title: Extending proper base change from $\Dctf$ to the localizing closure
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and let all schemes below be separated and of finite type over $k$, and all arrows be $k$-morphisms. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring as in [sk-def-localizing-closure], with the finite-subextension convention for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ in [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. For a scheme $T$ use the ordinary unbounded category $D(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$, its bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$, and its localizing closure $\Loc(\Dctf(T,\Lambda))$ [sk-def-localizing-closure].

Consider a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
p'\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$
with $p$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Write $u^*$ for the exact module-object inverse image [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], also applied termwise on derived categories, and $Ru_*$ for the total right derived module-object pushforward, with adjunction $u^*\dashv Ru_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $\theta:p'^*g^*\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^*p^*$ be induced termwise by the two module pullback composition isomorphisms [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] and the equality $g\circ p'=p\circ g'$. Let $\eta'$ be the unit for $p'^*\dashv Rp'_*$ and $\varepsilon$ the counit for $p^*\dashv Rp_*$. Define the base change map by
$$
\beta_K:
 g^*Rp_*K\xrightarrow{\eta'_{g^*Rp_*K}}
 Rp'_*p'^*g^*Rp_*K\xrightarrow{Rp'_*(\theta_{Rp_*K})}
 Rp'_*g'^*p^*Rp_*K\xrightarrow{Rp'_*g'^*(\varepsilon_K)}Rp'_*g'^*K.
$$
If $\beta_K$ is an isomorphism for every $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, then it is an isomorphism for every $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal L_T=\Loc(\Dctf(T,\Lambda))$. The cartesian identification $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] give properness of $p'$. All four schemes and both proper maps are in the standing setting, and all coefficient cases in [det-proper-image-localizing-proper] apply. Thus $Rp_*$ maps $\mathcal L_X$ into $\mathcal L_Y$, and $Rp'_*$ maps $\mathcal L_{X'}$ into $\mathcal L_{Y'}$, preserving all small ambient coproducts of objects in these source subcategories. Apply [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback] to $g$ and $g'$: their pullbacks map the corresponding localizing categories into each other and preserve sums. Consequently the underlying functors $F_1=g^*Rp_*$ and $F_2=Rp'_*g'^*$ map $\mathcal L_X$ to $\mathcal L_{Y'}$ and preserve sums. Indeed each composite sum comparison is the composite of the two constituent sum comparisons. The coproducts in these full subcategories are the ambient coproducts: they lie in the subcategory by [sk-def-localizing-closure], and its fullness gives the same universal property.

source.place: First two sentences: proper image and pullback restrictions; properness under base change is Stacks Tag 01W4 (morphisms.tex, lemma-base-change-proper).

proof.text: Use the usual termwise coherent integer-shift structures on inverse images. Their ambient derived functors are exact by [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback], applied also to $p$ and $p'$. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] the ambient derived adjunctions are $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$ and $Lp'^*\dashv Rp'_*$. The sheaf pullbacks are exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], so the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] gives canonical isomorphisms $Lu^*\cong D(u^*)$ with the termwise functors; transporting along them gives the adjunctions $p^*\dashv Rp_*$ and $p'^*\dashv Rp'_*$ of the statement, whose unit and counit are the $\eta'$ and $\varepsilon$ used in $\beta$. Apply clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique] to each adjunction to equip its right adjoint with the coherent shift structure compatible with that very unit and counit. Then [lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint] gives ambient exactness of each right adjoint with these structures. By Step 1 they map the relevant localizing subcategories into each other, so [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-restriction] gives their exact restrictions. The inverse images already have exact restrictions. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite] makes $F_1,F_2$ exact with the composite shift structures. Choosing these auxiliary shifts changes neither the underlying functors, the adjunction maps, the sum comparisons of Step 1, nor the morphism $\beta_K$ in the statement; invertibility of that morphism is independent of the auxiliary shift structures.

source.place: Third sentence, compatibility of units and counits. Details supplied from Stacks Tag 0A8D (derived.tex, lemma-adjoint-is-exact) and the existing abstract Mathlib leaves for compatible adjoint shifts, exact restriction and composition (Tags 05QX and 014Y).

proof.text: Let $\theta^0:p'^*g^*\cong g'^*p^*$ be the isomorphism on module sheaves obtained from [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] and the commutativity of the square. The sheaf pullbacks are exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], and their derived functors are the termwise functors $D(u^*)$ by the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For a representing complex $M^\bullet$, the degree-$r$ component of $\theta^0_{M[1]}$ is $\theta^0_{M^{r+1}}$, which is also the degree-$r$ component of $(\theta^0_M)[1]$. Additivity respects the negative differential of the shifted complex. Thus, with the composite termwise shifts, the comparison commutes with $[1]$ as a chain-map equality, and the same equality holds for every integer shift. Applying the localization functor, which commutes with shifts by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], gives shift compatibility of the specified $\theta$. This is a degreewise equality for any natural transformation between these exact termwise composites; it requires no preservation of K-injectives by inverse image.

source.place: Third sentence, connection isomorphism: explicit degreewise verification for the termwise comparison in the unit statement; shifts and localization as in Stacks Tag 05RU (derived.tex, definition-unbounded-derived-category).

proof.text: The unit $\eta'$ and counit $\varepsilon$ commute with the shifts chosen in Step 2, by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique]. The middle comparison commutes with shifts by Step 3. Apply the composition and whiskering clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] to the three natural transformations in the displayed definition of $\beta$. Their composite is a shift-compatible natural transformation $F_1\to F_2$. Since the target localizing category is full, this ambient natural transformation restricts componentwise to the exact functors of Step 2. Explicitly, writing $\sigma_i:F_i(K[1])\cong F_i(K)[1]$ for the composite shifts, its compatibility is $\sigma_{2,K}\circ\beta_{K[1]}=\beta_K[1]\circ\sigma_{1,K}$. This is the natural transformation of exact functors required by the determination lemma.

source.place: Third sentence: combine the verified unit, comparison and counit compatibilities; no geometric base-change theorem is used here.

proof.text: Apply [sk-lem-sf-determination] with source scheme $X$, target scheme $Y'$, the admissible coefficient $\Lambda$, the exact sum-preserving functors $F_1,F_2$ from Steps 1 and 2, and the shift-compatible natural transformation $\beta$ from Step 4. Its hypothesis on every $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is exactly the hypothesis of this item. The conclusion is that $\beta_K$ is an isomorphism for every $K\in\mathcal L_X=\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$.

source.place: Final sentence: determination on the localizing closure, with all hypotheses discharged in the preceding steps.

proof_origin.place: Whole proof paragraph, with the abstract adjunction-compatible shift construction (Stacks Tag 0A8D) and degreewise comparison calculation made explicit.

statement_correction.reason: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the imported reference to the unit leaves the standing scheme hypotheses absent from its standalone statement and its statement dependencies. The proper-image coefficient assertions used by its proof require separated finite-type schemes over the standing positive-characteristic field. Properness alone does not imply those hypotheses: the identity on an infinite disjoint union of Spec(k) is proper but its source is not finite type over k. This is a failing applicability check, not a claimed counterexample to base change. Explicitly restore the source chapter standing setting, as already done in the reviewed proper-image prerequisite; spell out the same ordinary unbounded base-change morphism without altering its generator assumption or conclusion.
